Virginia Tobacco Company (BD) Ltd  ------ Appellant
Vs
Registrar of Trade Marks and another ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 8. It appears from the impugned order that the respondent No. 1 did not at all conside the materials and grounds upon which the trade marks of the appellant as well as the respondent No. 2 were registered. It further appears that the impugned order does not show how, if any, the provision of sections 8(a) and 10(1) of the Act has been contravened in registering the trade mark of the appellant. It further appears that although it has been contended by the respondent No. 2 that due to registration of the mark of the appellant they have suffered material damage but there is no materials on record to show that they have, in fact, suffered materially or financially in their business due to the registration of the trade mark of the appellant. We also made an attempt to see if there is any similarity or dissimilarity between the mark of the appellant with that of the respondent No. 2 but find that sufficient materials have not been incorporated in the Paper Book. The original order by which the trade mark of the appellant was registered has also not been incorporated in the Paper Book nor the order of registration of the respondent No.2 is in the Record. Thus, we find that due to insufficiency of materials it is difficult for us to dispose of the appeal on merit and for the reasons assigned earlier it appears to us that the impugned order cannot be sustained in law. In view of the facts and circumstances of the case, it appears to be a fit case which should be sent back on remand to the Registrar of Trade Marks to dispose of the rectification application afresh after taking into consideration the Original Order of allowing the registration of the trade mark of the appellant as well as of the respondent No.2 and in disposing the application the Registrar should also take into consideration the provisions of sections 6, 8, 10, 13 and 46 of the Act and consider the said sections in the light of the scheme of the Act, The learned Registrar should also examine the question as to whether in rectification proceedings the question of validity of registration can be raised which could be properly examined when application for registration was originally moved. The Registrar also should take into consideration the issue of limitation.
